title: A small world, built together.
intro: Aussies in SF helps Australians living in or visiting the Bay Area find one another. It’s an open-source community project.

sections.heading: Suburbs, never addresses
sections.body: Every pin represents the centre of a neighbourhood. We don’t collect your exact address or GPS location. Publishing a profile shares your name, job description, suburb, LinkedIn link, contact email and visitor dates with people who can access this directory.

sections.heading: Coming and going
sections.body: Resident profiles stay visible. Visitors appear from their arrival date through their departure date, inclusive. Dates use UTC. Sign in and submit the join form again to update your profile.

sections.heading: Looking after the community
sections.body: Members self-identify as Australian; this is not a nationality verification service. Three different signed-in directory members reporting a profile will hide it for seven days. Duplicate reports and self-reports don’t count. Editing a profile doesn’t remove a suspension. Automatic reporting can be abused; a human moderation and appeal workflow is still needed before a broad launch.

sections.heading: Your profile, your choice
sections.body: You can remove your profile at any time while signed in. Minimal report records are retained to prevent repeat reporting.

sections.heading: Build it with us
sections.body: Code is MIT licensed. Contributions, issues and thoughtful suggestions are welcome.

sections.heading: What’s in this first version
sections.body: Shared profiles and reporting use a hosted database. ChatGPT sign-in identifies members. LinkedIn links are supported; automatic LinkedIn name/photo importing is not connected. Only real member profiles appear on the map; initials stand in for profile photos.
